text: Every tab across the top of a Lightning app — Home, Accounts, Opportunities, Reports — is configured in exactly one place: the Navigation Items step of that app. This lesson is about how an admin sets that default, and how far a user can personalize it from there.

Building or editing an app, Navigation Items shows two columns: Available Items on the left, Selected Items on the right. Moving an item across and reordering it with the arrows sets exactly what every user of that app sees by default — and order matters, because items render left to right in that sequence.
Here's what that configuration looks like live: the Sales app's navigation leads with Opportunities and Leads, the objects a rep lives in day to day.

Compare that to the Product Management app — Home, Products, Opportunities, Reports, Dashboards. Same org, same underlying data, completely different default navigation, because it's a different app with its own Navigation Items configuration.

Users aren't locked into the admin's exact order. They can drag items to reorder, add more from their favorites, and remove anything they added themselves. What they can't do is rename or remove the admin's default items — and past 50 items on a bar, personalization stops working at all.
Next up: the Utility Bar and Console Apps, where navigation gets a second, docked layer built for high-volume, multi-record work.
